name: The First Corner
narrative: The corridor ahead ends in a wall. If the robot only knows how to move forward, it will walk until it hits that wall and then freeze — paralysed because it has no rule for what to do next. Walls are not failures; they are information. You need to teach the robot that when the path ahead is blocked, it should turn and look for an open direction. This is the moment a robot stops being a projectile and starts being a navigator.
objective: Guide the robot around the corner to the goal and hold there for 3 ticks.
learningObjective: Writing multiple rules with different priorities, and using the `wallAhead` condition to react to the environment.
intelligenceExplanation: This brain already has one rule: move forward if the path is clear. But when the robot reaches the wall at the end of the corridor, no rule fires — it stalls. Add a second rule that handles the wall case and place it before the general movement rule. Arriving is not enough: the robot must stay on the goal tile for 3 consecutive ticks to confirm the arrival, so put WHEN atGoal -> DO hold first.
hint: Add a second rule: when `wallAhead`, do `pivot-right`. Place it above the move-forward rule so turning takes precedence.

rules.description: Move forward when the path is clear.
